events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.40)
events.body:
The trip was billed 21.66 km against a 15.9 km optimal route, a deviation of 5.78 km, above the 1 km tolerance [F1][F4][RD-1]. One off-route segment is on record: 17:31–17:43, 7.07 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.72 km, adding 5.35 km [F3]. The trace settles the RD-4 screen: no incident or congestion on the replaced stretch, so no traffic reason excuses the reroute [F3][F13][RD-4]. The trace also settles that no rider message before 17:31:20 agrees to the route, and the driver's post-trip statement is a claim, not consent [F7][F10][RD-5]. The only rider message is a challenge ("Why are we going this way? This is not the route on the app.") sent at 17:35, after the segment began [F7][F3], so the segment counts under RD-2: (5.78 km deviation − 0 exempt km) × $1.4100/km = $8.15, the excess distance billed [F4][RD-2].

However, the safety screen is decisive here. The rider's complaint says the driver "told me to shut up" and that the rider "felt unsafe", and the chat confirms the driver wrote "Shut up and let me drive." [F8]. Read in context, this is not a route remark but hostile language aimed at the rider during the trip — abuse under Ryde's code of conduct and a matter for SAFE-1, and the rider's statement of feeling unsafe reinforces it. Under SAFE-1 and SAFE-3 I therefore do not rule on the merits: the case goes to a human reviewer with a factual summary, and no fault is assigned and no outcome recommended.

Because the safety escalation is taken, I do not issue the segment ruling as the operative outcome; the arithmetic above is recorded for the reviewer's file. The element that is undetermined for the record before the reviewer is whether the rider's message at 17:35 modified the route (it can only be read as a challenge, [F7]) and whether the driver's "GPS rerouted" claim [F10] can be checked against the driver's own app data — the case file should include that.
